Welcome
Welcome
Welcome to Holy Trinity Primary School
Welcome to the Holy Trinity Primary School website. We are a warm, inclusive and welcoming school, proudly located in the heart of Dalston.
We are extremely proud of our school. Holy Trinity’s light-filled, state-of-the-art building is home to both our Preschool and our Church of England Primary School. Our Preschool welcomes babies from 6 months to 2 years, while our Primary School, including Nursery, educates children from 3 to 11 years of age. We are one of seven schools within the Primary Advantage Federation, led by our Executive Principal, Ms Davies.
Holy Trinity is a culturally and ethnically diverse school, and we are proud to reflect the rich community we serve. Every child at Holy Trinity is known, valued and supported to thrive. Through an engaging, inclusive curriculum, we prepare, inspire and empower all pupils to achieve their very best. Our expectations that children are Ready, Respectful and Safe underpin everything we do, supporting pupils to develop confidence, resilience and a reflective approach to learning and helping guide them to shine their light in all they do.
We are passionate about providing high-quality learning experiences and are committed to continually developing and improving our practice so that every child can achieve the best possible outcomes. Our Christian ethos is woven throughout school life, and our core values of Faith, Compassion, Endurance and Respect guide our work and prepare our pupils for the future.
Our website is regularly updated, and I encourage you to explore our weekly newsletters for a snapshot of life across the school. You can find our newsletters here.
If you are unable to find the information you are looking for, please do not hesitate to contact us. If you would like to experience Holy Trinity first-hand, I would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school. Please contact the school office on 0207 254 1010 to arrange a visit.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Values and Priorities
Vision, Values and Priorities
Every Learner: Empowered. Inspired. Prepared.
Vision
We aspire to be a confident community where all are nurtured and deeply valued for who they are, as beloved children of God.
Learners at Holy Trinity are:
Empowered by being given the tools they need in order to shine their light,
Inspired by the teachings of Jesus
Prepared for the future through the key Christian values of: faith, compassion, endurance and respect.
Our learning community seeks to foster these values, so that we might let God’s light shine through us in all that we do.
“You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hid. No one after lighting a lamp puts it under a basket, but on the lamp stand, and it gives light to all. In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your father in heaven.” Matthew 5:14-16*
Key Priorities
At Holy Trinity we evaluate all areas of school life as part of our continuing improvement journey. We use a wide range of evidence as well as end of key stage data to set our key priorities each year. We work with children, parents, governors and teachers to decide upon and share our goals for each academic year.
There are key priorities set for the Primary Advantage Federation, for Holy Trinity and for each curriculum area. The ambition is to meet these targets within the academic year.
If you would like a full copy of our School Development Plan please ask at the main office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity Primary School |   Our Church
pageCache.text:
Our Church
Our Church
The school enjoys an active partnership with our local parish church, Holy Trinity. We have a daily act of Christian collective worship for the whole school community. Collective worship is inclusive, invitational and inspiring and designed to support and contribute to the spiritual flourishing of all
Collective worship is rooted in our Christian vision and is designed to be invitational and inspirational, enabling pupils and adults to flourish spiritually, emotionally and socially. We aim to teach children about the beliefs and customs of other faiths, to foster sensitivity and understanding towards those whose religion and cultures are different from their own.
Worship follows a familiar structure which is accessible to all, regardless of academic ability, special educational need, faith or background. This consistency is designed to provide security and belonging and to support pupils to engage confidently and meaningfully. Inclusive language, accessible prayers and varied types of participation ensure that pupils of all faiths and none can engage in worship. Each act of worship begins with a shared call-and-response prayer and pupils are invited to light the candle, which symbolises Jesus as the Light of the World and our shared aspiration to reflect that light through our actions and attitudes. Each collective worship includes a Bible teaching, the school verse, a hymn and prayer. Time is intentionally built in for stillness, reflection and personal response, allowing pupils to consider their own relationship with God, their inner life and their place in the world. Pupils are encouraged to ask ‘big questions’ and to engage with the mystery and majesty of God, fostering awe and wonder.
Clergy-led worship takes place weekly, with further worship in church for significant points in the liturgical calendar, such as Easter, Christmas and Candlemas. Monthly Holy Moly family services strengthen links between school, church and families, supporting pupils’ spiritual development beyond the school day. Holy Moly services are usually on the first Wednesday of the month, and our school choir performs at each service. Places in the school choir are free on a first-come, first-served basis.
We follow the Collective Worship Calendar, based on the Lectionary.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity Primary School |   Spanish: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
pageCache.text:
Spanish: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Spanish: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Learning Spanish helps pupils broaden their horizons and deepen their understanding of the world. It opens the door to new cultures, new experiences and ways of communicating in an increasingly connected global community. We aim to foster a love of languages and help children develop the confidence to speak, listen, read and write in Spanish from an early age.
At Holy Trinity, we provide engaging, interactive lessons which develop pupils’ linguistic skills while maintaining enthusiasm and enjoyment. Language learning begins in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) through informal sessions, songs, stories and educational games. This learning journey continues progressively throughout pupils’ time at Holy Trinity. From Key Stage 2, the teaching of a modern foreign language becomes statutory. At this stage, pupils develop their understanding of basic grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation and listening skills, building the foundations needed for further language study.
Our Intent
Our Spanish curriculum is designed to ensure that pupils:
Develop accurate pronunciation and intonation
Build a secure and progressive vocabulary
Understand basic grammar, including gender, agreement and simple verb forms
Engage in conversations and express ideas confidently
Read and understand short texts
Write simple sentences and phrases from memory
We want children to leave primary school with a strong foundation in Spanish and the confidence to continue language learning at secondary school.
Our Approach
Spanish is taught through engaging, interactive lessons that focus on speaking and listening as the foundation of language learning. Children learn through:
Songs, rhymes and stories
Partner conversations
Visual prompts and practical activities
Cultural exploration
Key vocabulary and grammar are revisited regularly to ensure knowledge is embedded and built upon year by year. Lessons are designed to be active, inclusive and enjoyable, encouraging all pupils to participate and take risks in their speaking.
Cultural Understanding
Language learning goes beyond vocabulary and grammar. Pupils explore the traditions, celebrations and daily life of Spanish-speaking countries. They may learn about festivals, food, music and geography, helping them understand and respect different cultures.
Through this cultural awareness, children develop empathy, global awareness and an appreciation of diversity.
Skills for the Future
Learning Spanish supports wider skills development, including memory, listening, problem-solving and confidence in communication. It also strengthens understanding of English grammar and vocabulary.
By the end of Year 6, pupils can understand and respond to spoken and written Spanish, take part in simple conversations, and write short phrases and sentences independently.
We are proud to provide a Spanish curriculum that inspires enthusiasm, builds confidence and prepares children for continued language learning in the future.

Half Term Music Camp
09 May Half Term Music Camp

Music
Music
As a church school, music forms an important part of our worship. We sing together in collective worship every day and for special celebrations we gather together as a school community and sing at our local church.
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. As pupils progress, they should develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to compose, and to listen with discrimination to the best in the musical canon. – National Curriculum 2014
Every child receives a weekly music lesson with their class teacher using a specialised scheme. These lessons focus on the aims of the National Curriculum, whilst also linking with topics the children are learning in their other lessons or focussing specifically on learning an instrument such as the recorder or percussion instruments. Many children participate in our school choirs and perform both in and out of school. We share our love of music as a whole school in daily collective worship, special performances such as Black History Month, Christmas and Easter.
Music Curriculum
Music Curriculum Map – Follow this link to see the journey the children travel through the Music curriculum here at Holy Trinity.
Use this link for the Music skills progression document.
Singing
We intend that all pupils have opportunities within the music curriculum that will not only develop their knowledge and skills within the subject but enable them to unlock their innate creativity, in particular singing. We recognise the benefits that choral singing has:
Singing at Holy Trinity is part of our daily life. Since September 2021 we have been lucky enough to have teamed up with the Rodolfus Foundation https://www.therodolfusfoundation.org.uk/choral-academy-hackney to provide our pupils with weekly choral singing lessons with a specialist teacher. The change in school has been dramatic in terms of how singing lessons are participated in and the enjoyment that we are all taking from the lessons, we look forward to exploring new opportunities together in the future. Themes within the subject are linked to other curriculum areas where possible.
improving mood and focus’ attention

Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
View information about our Breakfast Club here.
Our Breakfast Club operates between 8:00 a.m. and 8:45 a.m. Children should arrive no earlier than 8:00 a.m. and before 8:30 a.m. so that they don’t miss the breakfast serving.
Breakfast club will start each term on the day that the main school returns.
£25.00 per child per week
£25.00 per child per week
£12.50 per child per week
For children in Reception and Years 1 – 6, a payment must be made at the beginning of each week through ParentPay. Payment must still be paid if your child does not attend due to sickness or any other reason. If payments fall into arrears, places will be reallocated.
When breakfast club is full there is a waiting list for children who would like to be considered in the future. Please click here to fill in a form to be placed into breakfast club or to be placed on the waiting list in the event that it is full.

Parent Teacher Association Meetings this Half Term
26 Feb Parent Teacher Association Meetings this Half Term
If you would like to be a part of the Parent Teacher Association (PTA), we are having meetings on Wednesday 6th March at 9:00 and Wednesday 13th March at 3:30.
It will be an opportunity for us to discuss upcoming events in the next few months for the school and future fundraising opportunities. Please also let us know if you would like to offer your support at the Easter Bake Off on Friday 19th April 3:45-5:00.
